players.product: AI data-center campus leases on converted Bitcoin-mining power sites (Sandersville GA 175 MW critical IT on a 20-year triple net lease, tenant undisclosed; Sealy and Brazoria TX under exclusivity)

quarterly_data.signal: CleanSpark's 10-K: its one mining pool operator, Foundry Digital, represented 100% of the company's total revenues in fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023, as all bitcoin mining rewards are received through Foundry Digital's open access mining pool; rewards are distributed proportionally to CleanSpark's contribution to the pool's mining power, and the pool has sole discretion to modify the terms of the agreement at any time. Bitcoin mining revenues are recorded net of the pool fees charged by Foundry, approximately 0.17% of gross bitcoin mining revenues in fiscal 2025 (0.16% in fiscal 2024). All of its bitcoin reside with one custodian.
quarterly_data.figure: Foundry Digital 100% of revenue (fiscal 2025, 2024, 2023); pool fees ~0.17% of gross mining revenue (fiscal 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: CleanSpark's 10-K: it relies on a limited number of suppliers for the purchase and delivery of its miners and depends on Bitmain, MicroBT, Canaan Crypt Solutions and Sunnyside Digital for its miners; supply chain disruptions from tariffs, inflation, labor supply and shipping container shortages have impacted, and may continue to impact, the company and its manufacturers. Its contractual obligations primarily consist of cancelable purchase commitments, primarily for miners and equipment. Payments on miners and mining equipment (including deposits) were $418,212 thousand in fiscal 2025 versus $740,296 thousand in fiscal 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: Miner and mining-equipment payments $418,212 thousand (fiscal 2025) vs $740,296 thousand (fiscal 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: CleanSpark's 10-K: miners in operation rose to 241,934 as of September 30, 2025 from 188,500 as of September 30, 2024 (+28%), increasing its hashrate. It mined 7,873 bitcoins in fiscal 2025, gross of Foundry fees, at an average bitcoin price of $97,337, versus 7,092 bitcoins at $53,434 in fiscal 2024. Owned facilities mined 7,726 bitcoin for $754,691 thousand of bitcoin mining revenue, using 5,859,543,539 kWh at $0.057 per kWh (energy expense 43.9% of net mining revenue); the direct energy cost to mine one bitcoin was $42,956 and $82,727 including miner depreciation and financing costs, against average revenue of $97,687 per bitcoin mined. Hosted facilities mined 147 bitcoin for $11,623 thousand, with no miners in service there at year end.
quarterly_data.figure: 241,934 miners (+28%); 7,873 bitcoin mined (fiscal 2025); $0.057 per kWh; $82,727 cost to mine per bitcoin (owned facilities)

quarterly_data.signal: CleanSpark's 10-K calls itself a data center developer, until recently focused exclusively on bitcoin mining. It owns and leases air-cooled bitcoin mining facilities in Georgia, Mississippi and Tennessee, owns an immersion bitcoin mining property in College Park, Georgia and two immersion bitcoin mining facilities in Cheyenne, Wyoming. Its hosting agreement at an independent data center in Massena, NY that operated 50 MW expired on December 31, 2024, and all MW allocated to the company were vacated as of September 30, 2025. It produced 612 bitcoin in October 2025 and has no intention to mine, purchase or hold any other crypto assets.
quarterly_data.figure: 612 bitcoin produced (October 2025); 50 MW Massena, NY hosting ended
